title: Scientific Simulation Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Simulation models, initial conditions, assumptions, results, and reproducibility records. The Scientific Simulation Database records computational experiments as first-class science: the model (equations + discretization), initial and boundary conditions, every assumption made, the results, and the reproducibility package that lets anyone re-run it. A simulation without its assumptions documented is a story, not science — each record makes the model, the conditions, and the limits explicit so results can be trusted, challenged, and built upon.

title: Scientific Simulation Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Simulation anatomy: continuous model (PDEs/ODEs from physics) -> discretization (finite difference/volume/element; grid or particles) -> solver (explicit/implicit time stepping; linear solvers) -> analysis (convergence, validation). Key numbers: CFL condition for explicit schemes (dt <= dx/c); order of accuracy (error ~ h^p); convergence study (refine mesh, watch the answer stabilize — Richardson extrapolation estimates the limit). Verification vs validation: verification (solving the equations right — manufactured solutions), validation (solving the right equations — compare to experiment). Assumption classes: geometric (symmetry, dimensionality), physical (neglected forces, material models), numerical (resolution, tolerances). Uncertainty: input uncertainty propagates to output bands (see UQ database).

demo.title: Execution: numerical integration vs analytic
demo.code: function trap(f,a,b,n){const h=(b-a)/n;let s=(f(a)+f(b))/2;for(let i=1;i<n;i++)s+=f(a+i*h);return s*h;}const num=trap(x=>x*x,0,2,10000);const exact=8/3;const err=Math.abs(num-exact);J({num:+num.toFixed(6),exact:+exact.toFixed(6),err:+err.toExponential(1)});assert(err<1e-6,'integration');

title: Scientific Simulation Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: convergence test (error shrinks at the theoretical order); conservation test (conserved quantities stay constant); replay test (package reproduces results bit-for-bit); assumption test (every record has a non-empty assumption log). Limitations: demos use simple models; real multiphysics needs HPC; validation against experiment is the gold standard and is recorded when available. Every result carries its resolution and uncertainty.

demo.title: Verification: BFS shortest path
demo.code: const g={a:['b','c'],b:['a','d'],c:['a','d'],d:['b','c','e'],e:['d']};function bfs(s,t){const q=[[s]],seen=new Set([s]);while(q.length){const p=q.shift();const n=p[p.length-1];if(n===t)return p;for(const m of g[n])if(!seen.has(m)){seen.add(m);q.push([...p,m]);}}}const path=bfs('a','e');J({path});assert(JSON.stringify(path)==='["a","b","d","e"]','bfs');

demo.title: Verification: uncertainty propagation analytic vs Monte Carlo
demo.code: let seed=7;function rnd(){seed=(seed*1103515245+12345)&0x7fffffff;return seed/0x7fffffff;}const L=10,sL=0.2,W=5,sW=0.1;const analytic=L*W*Math.sqrt((sL/L)**2+(sW/W)**2);let sum=0,sum2=0,N=50000;for(let i=0;i<N;i++){const l=L+sL*(rnd()+rnd()+rnd()-1.5)*2;const w=W+sW*(rnd()+rnd()+rnd()-1.5)*2;const a=l*w;sum+=a;sum2+=a*a;}const mc=Math.sqrt(sum2/N-(sum/N)**2);J({analytic:+analytic.toFixed(3),mc:+mc.toFixed(3)});assert(Math.abs(analytic-mc)<0.15,'uq');

demo.title: Connection: simulation convergence study
demo.code: function sim(dt){let y=0,vy=50*Math.sin(Math.PI/6);const g=9.81;const T=5;for(let t=0;t<T;t+=dt){vy-=g*dt;y+=vy*dt;}return y;}const exact=50*Math.sin(Math.PI/6)*5-0.5*9.81*25;const e1=Math.abs(sim(0.02)-exact),e2=Math.abs(sim(0.01)-exact),e3=Math.abs(sim(0.005)-exact);const order=Math.log2(e1/e2);J({exact:+exact.toFixed(3),e1:+e1.toExponential(2),e2:+e2.toExponential(2),order:+order.toFixed(2)});assert(order>0.8&&order<1.3,'convergence');
